decisions.decision: A bare noun is grammatically number-neutral by default. It may denote one or more referents when context supplies the intended number. Nominal plural marking is optional and informative rather than obligatory.

Use the invariant pre-nominal particle wi as the optional explicit nominal plural marker. Canonical form /wi/; accepted accent-tolerant realization [u̯i] may be used where /w/ is not stable. Wi marks plurality only: it does not mark definiteness, gender, or agreement.

Normally omit wi when plurality or quantity is already explicit through a numeral or quantifier. Thus ter om means three people and omni om means all/every person or all people; redundant wi is not required.

Use invariant pre-nominal omni for universal quantification over members of a set: ALL / EVERY. It may receive collective or distributive interpretation from context. Examples: omni om 'all people / every person'; tik omni om 'all these people'; tan omni om 'all those people'.

Use invariant pre-nominal tot for the total integrity or entirety of one referent or mass: WHOLE / ENTIRE. It is not the ordinary set-universal quantifier. Examples: tot dom 'the whole house'; tot dia 'the whole day'; tot mund 'the whole world'.
When a demonstrative and a quantifier co-occur, the demonstrative precedes the quantifier, which precedes the noun: tik omni om; tes omni om; tan omni om.
Keep mi unassigned for now. It is reserved as a strong phonological form for a possible future grammatical function, but currently has no canonical meaning.

Use invariant pre-nominal nul for ZERO / NO quantity. It means that the set contains no referents: nul om 'no person / nobody'; nul omo 'no man'; nul ome 'no woman'; nul dom 'no house'. Because nul already fixes quantity at zero, wi is not used with it.
Use invariant free si for YES and no for NO. The same free form no also serves as the pre-verbal sentential negator NOT; ka remains the separate polar-question marker.

Use hyphenated enclitic -si for additive focus ALSO / TOO (Italian anche / pure). It attaches to the right edge of the focused constituent: i-si 'I too'; tik om-si 'this person too'. Free si 'YES' and bound -si are distinguished by syntax and orthography.

Use hyphenated enclitic -no for negative-additive focus NEITHER / NOT EVEN / NOT ... EITHER (Italian neanche / nemmeno). It attaches to the right edge of the focused constituent: i-no vidi 'not even I see'; dom-no 'not even the house'. Bound -no itself supplies clause-negative polarity for this ordinary reading, so an additional pre-verbal no is not required.

The focus enclitics -si and -no scope over the constituent whose right edge hosts them. In multiword nominal constituents the clitic is written on the final word: tik omni om-si 'all these people too'; tik omni om-no 'not even all these people'.

Use genitive -s by default and -es after stems ending in s, z, sj, tj, or dj. A stem ending in ts is covered by the final-s trigger. The support vowel preserves pronounceability for canonical sibilant edges and for sj/tj/dj when they surface coalescently as [sh]/[tsh]/[dzh]. Plain final j is the glide /j/ and does not by itself trigger -es.

Form personal possessives productively as genitives of the confirmed personal pronouns: i->is, u->us, a->as, in->ins, un->uns, an->ans. They are invariant and do not agree with the possessed noun. Optional third-person referential specificity remains inside the pronoun before genitive -s: ao->aos, ae->aes, ano->anos, ane->anes; neutral as/ans always remain valid.

Keep copula/existential root es. In the current person-number system its present explicit forms are esi, esu, esa, esin, esun, esan. Present-simple adjectival, nominal, and locative predicates may use zero copula; explicit es is available for emphasis/existence and supplies the verbal carrier when TAM is required. Existing TAM markers precede the current person vowel plus optional plural N, e.g. esdi/esdu/esda/esdin/esdun/esdan for simple past and esfi/esfu/esfa/esfin/esfun/esfan for simple future.
